newsitem.title: USA: CBS roving reporter Charles Kuralt dies at 62.
newsitem.headline: CBS roving reporter Charles Kuralt dies at 62.

text.p: Veteran CBS television and radio newsman Charles Kuralt, known for his offbeat "On The Road" reports, died early Friday at a New York City hospital, CBS said. He was 62.
Kuralt died of complications from lupus, a progressive disease of the auto-immune system, a hospital spokesman said.

He joined CBS in 1957 and in recent years had anchored the network's "Sunday Morning" news magazine show. During his trademark "On The Road" reports, Kuralt logged more than a million miles chronicling the lives of Americans.

"He was one of the true greatly talented people in television. He loved the country, he loved travelling," fellow CBS journalist Walter Cronkite, vacationing on the Massachusetts coast, told Boston's WBZ radio station after learning of Kuralt's death.
"I'm terribly shocked ... I didn't have any idea Charles was in mortal danger. There probably wasn't any more of a patriotic or loving man in television or the country than Charles," Cronkite said.
CNN's Washington bureau chief Frank Sesno, speaking to reporters at an Independence Day celebration in Philadelphia, called Kuralt a "poet."
"The chronicle of the country and the nation that he brought was among the most beautiful and vivid journalism that I've ever heard in broadcast," Sesno said.

"He created an art form, really, in television broadcast. He was one of the best writers that television has ever known. His voice, his inflection, his delivery. Everything about him was just pure art, I must say. I missed him since he retired. We'll miss his presence and his grace."

Kuralt was born Sept. 10, 1934, in Wilmington, N.C. As a high school student, he won the American Legion essay contest and a trip to Washington to meet President Truman. After graduation from the University of North Carolina, where he edited the campus newspaper, Kuralt joined CBS.
